pluss::timeline::from_epoch¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::from_epoch(std::int64_t value,
                                     std::string_view timezone = "UTC")
Timeline pluss::timeline::from_epoch(integer_data values,
                                     std::string_view timezone = "UTC")
Timeline pluss::timeline::from_epoch(integer_range flat, integer_range sizes,
                                     std::string_view timezone = "UTC")
Timeline pluss::timeline::from_epoch(const Series& values,
                                     std::string_view timezone = "UTC")

Preserve Exact Epoch Nanoseconds¶

from_epoch() is the lossless integer entrance to Timeline. Every value is interpreted as a signed count of nanoseconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000000Z. Positive values follow the epoch, negative values precede it, and zero is the epoch itself.

Use this factory for database ticks, binary protocols, memory-mapped integer columns, or a round trip through epoch_nanos(). It never passes values through floating point, so adjacent nanoseconds remain distinct even beyond the exact integer range of a binary floating representation.

timezone is presentation metadata. It changes which civil fields and offset are displayed, but not the supplied ticks. The name is validated immediately. The reserved value Timeline::kNaT deliberately creates an absent instant; every other signed 64-bit tick is an instant.

The Series overload is the shape-preserving bridge from numeric work into temporal work. Its dtype must already be int64; the factory rejects other dtypes instead of silently truncating floating values or reinterpreting a different integer width. Noncontiguous input is read in logical row-major order, and the resulting Timeline owns its epoch data independently.

Example 1: Exactness Beyond 2^53¶

constexpr std::int64_t tick = 9'007'199'254'740'993LL;
const auto t = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(tick);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, t.epoch_nanos());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=9007199254740993

Scalar input creates a rank-zero timeline and returns the identical integer.

Example 2: Before, At, And Absent From The Epoch¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    {-1LL, 0LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(t, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["1969-12-31T23:59:59.999999999+00:00", "1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000000+00:00", "NaT"]

Negative nanoseconds use ordinary floor-based temporal meaning: -1 is the last nanosecond before the epoch, not a truncated zero.

Example 3: Nested Integer Geometry¶

const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::from_epoch({{0LL, 1LL}, {2LL, 3LL}});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, matrix.epoch_nanos());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 0 1 ⎤
⎣ 2 3 ⎦

Nested literals must be rectangular and may express up to rank three.

Example 4: Preserve A Series Shape¶

const auto ticks = pluss::make_series(
    {{std::int64_t{0}, std::int64_t{1}},
     {std::int64_t{2}, std::int64_t{3}}});
const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(ticks);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, matrix.epoch_nanos());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 0 1 ⎤
⎣ 2 3 ⎦

This overload preserves rank and shape; it does not flatten a matrix into a one-dimensional Timeline.

Example 5: A Timezone Changes The View, Not The Tick¶

const auto local =
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(0LL, "America/Edmonton");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(local, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"1969-12-31T17:00:00.000000000-07:00"

The local calendar shows the preceding date, but epoch_nanos() remains zero.

Example 6: Runtime Flat Data With Three-Dimensional Shape¶

const std::vector<std::int64_t> flat{0, 1, 2, 3};
const auto cube = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(flat, {1, 2, 2});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, cube.epoch_nanos());

Output¶

Series(shape=[1,2,2], strides=[4,2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data[0, :, :] =
⎡ 0 1 ⎤
⎣ 2 3 ⎦

The product of sizes must equal flat.size(). The factory copies values into contiguous owned storage; use the buffer bridge when existing strided storage must be shared instead.

Round Trips And Failures¶

from_epoch(t.epoch_nanos().to_vec<std::int64_t>(), t.sizes()) preserves every tick and shape, but the new timezone defaults to UTC unless supplied. Unknown timezone names, negative extents, rank above three, ragged nested input, and shape/cardinality mismatch throw before a usable result is returned.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeline::from_epoch(0LL, "Mars/Olympus_Mons");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected
